components.name: Square-basin rough-window recursion and high least-factor contraction
components.project_addition: Apply established rough-number and Buchstab least-factor recursion to exact finite cofactor windows forced by consecutive-square geometry; combine square-derived quotient transport with high-band contraction, binary second-factor branches, pairwise resource separation, multiplicative capacity, cross-shell hit-state unions, and finite/analytic high-band composite envelopes. In the complementary lower band p^2<2k, reuse canonical P018 two-basin quotient transport to prove a cross-shell packing theorem: the candidate descended root pair {j_p,j_p+1}, with j_p=R_2(floor(k^2/p)), has target multiplicity at most two across all lower-band least-prime shells. The lower-band packing proof is elementary integer arithmetic and prime spacing; no new external source is introduced. Historical novelty of these square-basin specializations remains unverified.
